title: Part 2: Cue Card — के हुन्छ र के चाहिन्छ
blocks: Part 1 सकिएपछि examiner ले यस्तो केही भन्नुहुन्छ: "Now I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish." त्यसपछि उहाँले तपाईंलाई एउटा card, एउटा कागज र एउटा pencil दिनुहुन्छ। Card यस्तो देखिन्छ:

**Describe a skill you learned from an older person.**
You should say:

  what the skill is

  who taught you and when

  how you learned it

and explain how you feel about having this skill now.

हरेक card-को बनावट एउटै हुन्छ: एउटा **मुख्य topic** (पहिलो लाइन), तीनवटा **bullet point** (के भन्ने भन्ने संकेत), र अन्त्यमा एउटा **"and explain..."** — जसले सधैं तपाईंको भावना, विचार वा कारण माग्छ। यो अन्तिम लाइन नै सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण हो, र सबैभन्दा धेरै बेवास्ता पनि यसैलाई गरिन्छ।

Part 2 परीक्षाको एउटै यस्तो भाग हो जहाँ तपाईं **एक्लै, लगातार र बीचमा कसैले नरोकी** बोल्नुहुन्छ। Part 1 मा छोटा प्रश्नहरूले तपाईंलाई सघाउँछन्; Part 3 मा examiner का प्रश्नहरूले बाटो देखाउँछन्। Part 2 मा बाटो तपाईं आफैंले तय गर्नुपर्छ। त्यसैले यहाँ examiner ले मुख्यतया यी कुरा हेर्नुहुन्छ:
के तपाईं **२ मिनेटसम्म** बोलिरहन सक्नुहुन्छ, कि ४५ सेकेन्डमै कुरा सकिन्छ?
के तपाईंको कुरा **कतै पुगिरहेको छ** — सुरु, बीच र अन्त्य छ — कि जताततै छरिएको छ?
के तपाईं **कथा भन्न** सक्नुहुन्छ — past tense, sequence, वर्णन, भावना?
के तपाईं **topic मै** हुनुहुन्छ, कि अर्कै कुरा (रटेको कुरा) भनिरहनुभएको छ?
**पूरा २ मिनेट भर्ने कोसिस गर्नुहोस्।** Examiner ले २ मिनेटमा तपाईंलाई रोक्नुहुन्छ — त्यो राम्रो संकेत हो। १ मिनेट नपुग्दै रोकिनुभयो भने FC score-मा सीधै असर पर्छ।
**रोकिँदा दुःखी नहुनुहोस्।** "...and that's when I— " "Thank you." — script नै यही हो। बीचमै रोकिनु भनेको तपाईंसँग भन्ने कुरा प्रशस्त थियो भन्ने हो।

**१ मिनेटको note का लागि पूरा समय प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्।** "I'm ready" भनेर चाँडै सुरु गर्नुको कुनै फाइदा छैन — उल्टो, घाटा हुन्छ। अहिलेको ६० सेकेन्डको सोचाइ भनेको २ मिनेटको talk-का बेला ६० सेकेन्ड कम सोच्नुपर्ने हो।

title: १ मिनेटको Note: के लेख्ने, के नलेख्ने
blocks: Note लेख्दा हुने सबैभन्दा ठूलो गल्ती हो **वाक्य लेख्नु**। एक मिनेटमा तपाईं बढीमा दुईवटा वाक्य लेख्न सक्नुहुन्छ, अनि ती दुई वाक्य पढेर सुनाउनुहुन्छ — बोल्ने होइन, पढ्ने। पढेको र बोलेको फरक examiner ले एकै सेकेन्डमा थाहा पाउनुहुन्छ।
दोस्रो गल्ती हो **केही पनि नलेख्नु** — "म दिमागमै राख्न सक्छु"। ९० सेकेन्ड पुग्दा, nervous भएको अवस्थामा, तपाईं आफ्नो तेस्रो point बिर्सनुहुन्छ।

Card-का चारवटा लाइन (तीन bullet + "explain") मध्ये हरेकका लागि **एउटा keyword** लेख्नुहोस्, साथै **एउटा थप** — जुन card ले मागेको छैन तर तपाईंको कथालाई वास्तविक बनाउँछ। जम्मा ५ वटा शब्द, ठूला अक्षरमा, एकमुनि अर्को गरी। माथिको card का लागि यस्तो हुन सक्छ:

SEWING — grandmother, Eid holidays, age 12

WATCH → PRACTISE → MISTAKES (crooked hem)

NOW: fix own clothes, save money

FEEL: proud, connected to her

+ old black machine, foot pedal sound

ध्यान दिनुहोस्: हरेक लाइन एक नजरमै पढ्न सकिन्छ, र हरेक शब्दबाट तपाईं २-३ वटा वाक्य निकाल्न सक्नुहुन्छ। अन्तिम लाइन (+) "sensory detail" हो — कुनै दृश्य, आवाज वा गन्ध, जसले कथालाई साँचो जस्तो बनाउँछ र तपाईंलाई vocabulary देखाउने मौका दिन्छ।
पूरै card पढ्नुहोस् — विशेष गरी अन्तिम लाइन। **एउटा** निश्चित कुरा/मान्छे/घटना छान्नुहोस्। दुईवटाबीच अलमलमा नपर्नुहोस्; दिमागमा पहिले जुन आउँछ, जसबारे भन्ने कुरा धेरै छ, त्यही लिनुहोस्।
४ वटा bullet का लागि ४ वटा keyword लेख्नुहोस्।
पहिलो वाक्य मनमनै भन्नुहोस्। सुरुआत ठीक भयो भने बाँकी आफैं आउँछ।

**Topic बारे साँचो कुरा:** "Describe a skill you learned from an older person" — यदि तपाईंसँग साँच्चै यस्तो केही छैन भने बनाएर भन्नुहोस्, वा नजिकको केही लिनुहोस् (साथीबाट सिकेको भए पनि "my older cousin" भन्नुहोस्)। Examiner ले साँचो हो कि होइन जाँच्नुहुन्न। तर **topic नबदल्नुहोस्** — skill को सट्टा journey बारे बोल्नु off-topic हो, र यसले तपाईंको FC score घटाउँछ।

title: २ मिनेटको Talk: बनावट
blocks: यही हो Tip #3 — "Master Part 2 Structure"। जुनसुकै cue card, जुनसुकै topic: उही पाँचवटा चरण। यो किताबमा तपाईंले रट्नुपर्ने एउटै कुरा यही हो — र यो रटिसकेपछि अरू केही रट्नु पर्दैन।
तपाईं केबारे बोल्दै हुनुहुन्छ — एक वाक्यमा, card को शब्दलाई paraphrase गरेर।
I'd like to talk about... / The [skill/place/person] I've chosen is... / OK, so this is about...
के, को, कहिले, कहाँ — पृष्ठभूमि। यहाँ past tense, र मान्छे/ठाउँको वर्णन।
This was back when... / It all started... / She was the kind of person who...
कसरी — चरणबद्ध रूपमा, एउटा सानो घटना, एउटा समस्या र त्यसको समाधान। कथा यहीँ हुन्छ।
At first... then... / The tricky part was... / I remember one time...
Card को अन्तिम लाइन। तपाईंलाई कस्तो लाग्छ, किन महत्त्वपूर्ण छ, के बदलियो। Present tense मा फर्कनुहोस्।
Looking back, ... / What it means to me now is... / The reason it matters is...
एक वाक्यमा टुंग्याउनुहोस् — भविष्य, वा मुख्य कुरा फेरि।
So, all in all... / That's why I'll always... / I suppose that's the story of...
Worked example: note देखि talk सम्म
माथिको note बाट बनेको पूरा talk। हरेक चरण चिनो लगाइएको छ। यो करिब २ मिनेटको छ — सामान्य गतिमा २८०-३०० शब्द।

**[1 Opening]** The skill I'd like to talk about is sewing, which I learned from my grandmother when I was about twelve.
**[2 Context]** This was during the long Eid holidays, when we'd go to stay at her house in the village for a couple of weeks. She had this ancient black sewing machine — the kind you work with a foot pedal — and I can still hear the rhythm of it, this steady clacking sound coming from the back room every afternoon. She was a very patient woman, but also quite strict about doing things properly, which turned out to be exactly what I needed.
**[3 Process]** At first she wouldn't let me touch the machine at all. For the first few days I just watched her, and then she gave me scraps of old cloth to practise straight lines on. The tricky part was keeping the pressure on the pedal steady — I remember my first hem came out completely crooked, and instead of fixing it for me, she made me unpick the whole thing and do it again. I was annoyed at the time, but by the end of the holiday I'd made a small cushion cover on my own.
**[4 Explain]** Looking back, I feel genuinely proud of having this skill, partly because so few people my age can do it. On a practical level, I fix my own clothes instead of throwing them away, which saves money and, honestly, feels quite satisfying. But more than that, every time I sit at a machine I feel connected to her — she passed away a few years ago, and this is the most tangible thing she left me.
**[5 Closing]** So I suppose it's much more than a skill to me; it's a bit of her that I still carry around.

Examiner ले खोज्ने के-के कुरा यो talk मा छन्: past narrative (was, wouldn't let, came out, made me), sensory detail (black machine, clacking sound), एउटा सानो समस्या र त्यसको समाधान (crooked hem), present tense मा reflection, precise vocabulary (ancient, steady, unpick, tangible), र स्पष्ट अन्त्य।

title: २ मिनेट भर्ने रणनीति
blocks: "मसँग भन्ने कुरै छैन" — Part 2 बारे सबैभन्दा धेरै सुनिने गुनासो यही हो, र यो प्रायः सधैं गलत हुन्छ। भन्ने कुरा छन्; तपाईंलाई कुन कोणबाट हेर्ने भन्ने मात्र थाहा छैन। तलका ६ वटा "lens" जुनसुकै topic मा लगाउनुहोस्, २ मिनेट त उल्टै छोटो लाग्छ।
पहिलो पटक कहिले? अहिले कस्तो छ? अब के हुन्छ?
First went there in 2nd year... now go every Thursday... will probably keep going after I graduate.
हेर्दा, सुन्दा, गन्ध र स्वाद कस्तो छ?
Dim yellow lights, smell of cardamom tea, old Bangla songs playing softly.
त्यहाँ को हुन्छन्? तपाईं कोसँग जानुहुन्छ?
The owner, who remembers everyone's order; my two closest friends.
अरूभन्दा कसरी फरक छ? पहिले त्यहाँ के थियो?
Unlike the chain cafés, nobody hurries you out; before it opened, there was nowhere to sit near campus.
कुनै एउटा खास दिनको सानो घटना?
The night we stayed until closing finishing a group project, and the owner brought us free tea.
तपाईंको जीवनमा यसको अर्थ के हो? यसले के बदल्यो?
It's where most of my university friendships were actually built.
Card का तीनवटा bullet ले सामान्यतया lens १, ३ र ५ समेट्छन्; "explain" लाइन lens ६ हो। बाँकी दुई (senses, contrast) तपाईंले आफैं थप्ने कुरा हुन् — र Band 6 लाई Band 7 बनाउने यिनै हुन्।
**आफ्नो note हेर्नुहोस्** — कुन keyword अझै प्रयोग गर्नुभएको छैन? त्यहाँ जानुहोस्: "Oh, and another thing I should mention is..."
**Lens बदल्नुहोस्**: अहिलेसम्म के भयो भनेर वर्णन गर्दै हुनुहुन्थ्यो → अब त्यसबारे कस्तो लाग्छ भन्नुहोस्। "Thinking about it now, ..."
**तुलना गर्नुहोस्**: "Compared to other [cafés/gifts/journeys] I've had, this one..."
**टुंग्याउनुहोस्** — १ मिनेट २० सेकेन्ड पार भइसकेपछि जबरजस्ती तन्काउनुभन्दा closing सहित राम्ररी रोकिनु राम्रो।
Part 2 को भाषा: कथा भन्ने toolkit
back in [year], a few years ago, when I was in my final year, at the time, around that period, it must have been [season]
to begin with, after a while, the next thing I knew, eventually, by the end of it, in the end
she was the kind of person who..., he had a way of..., what struck me about her was..., a bit of a [perfectionist / joker]
tucked away behind..., it's the sort of place where..., what makes it special is..., nothing fancy, but...
I was over the moon, I was a nervous wreck, I couldn't believe my luck, I was a bit taken aback, it was a real eye-opener
looking back, in hindsight, thinking about it now, it still makes me smile, I'll always be grateful for
the thing I remember most vividly is..., what really stood out was..., I'll never forget...
Card का bullet एक-एक गरी, हरेकमा एउटा मात्र वाक्य भनेर जानु ("The skill is sewing. My grandmother taught me. I learned by practising. I feel good.") — ३० सेकेन्डमै सकिन्छ।
हरेक bullet लाई २-४ वाक्यको एउटा paragraph सम्झनुहोस्। Lens प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्।
सामान्य कुरा गर्नु ("Sewing is a useful skill. Many people learn sewing...") — त्यो त Part 3 को भाषा हो।
Part 2 व्यक्तिगत र निश्चित हुन्छ: "I", "my", कुनै खास मान्छे, दिन वा ठाउँ।
Card सँग आंशिक रूपमा मात्र मिल्ने रटेको talk दिनु।
Examiner ले थाहा पाउनुहुन्छ र follow-up मा अर्कै प्रश्न सोध्नुहुन्छ। Content होइन, structure रट्नुहोस्।
बितेको कुराको कथामा present tense प्रयोग गर्नु ("Then she gives me cloth and I practise...")।
Note को छेउमा "PAST" लेख्नुहोस्। पहिलो वाक्य past मा सुरु गर्नुभयो भने बाँकी सजिलो हुन्छ।
Note एक झलक हेर्नका लागि मात्र हो; ८०% समय examiner तिर हेर्नुहोस्।
"Explain" लाइन छुटाउनु, वा एक वाक्यमै सक्नु।
यो ३० सेकेन्डको भाग हो, र सबैभन्दा राम्रो vocabulary (भावना, reflection) यहीँ आउँछ।

तपाईंको talk सकिएपछि examiner ले एक-दुईवटा छोटा प्रश्न सोध्न सक्नुहुन्छ: "Do you still sew?", "Would you teach this to someone?" यी Part 3 होइनन् — **एक-दुई वाक्यमा** उत्तर दिनुहोस्। लामो उत्तर दिनुभयो भने उहाँले रोक्नुहुन्छ।

title: Part 3: Discussion — खेल नै बदलिन्छ
blocks: Part 2 सकिएपछि examiner ले card फिर्ता लिनुहुन्छ र भन्नुहुन्छ: "We've been talking about a skill you learned from an older person, and I'd like to discuss with you one or two more general questions related to this." यही "more general" भन्ने शब्दमा Part 3 को सार छ। प्रश्नहरू अब तपाईंबारे होइनन् — **मान्छे, समाज, देश र भविष्य**-बारे हुन्छन्।
Describe a skill you learned from an older person.

What kinds of skills do older people typically pass on to younger generations? / Are traditional skills disappearing in your country? Why? / Should schools teach practical skills like cooking or repairing things? / In the future, will people learn more from other people or from the internet?

यही हो Tip #5 — "Handle Part 3 Abstract Questions"। Part 3 मा examiner ले तपाईं **विचार दिन, कारण बुझाउन, तुलना गर्न, अनुमान गर्न र दुवै पक्ष हेर्न** सक्नुहुन्छ कि सक्नुहुन्न भनेर हेर्न चाहनुहुन्छ — अर्थात् तपाईं अंग्रेजीमा **सोच्न** सक्नुहुन्छ कि सक्नुहुन्न। Vocabulary र grammar को range देखाउने सबैभन्दा ठूलो मौका यही हो, र Band 7 को धेरैजसो निर्णय यहीँ हुन्छ।
**"मैले सही उत्तर दिनुपर्छ।"** होइन। Examiner सँग कुनै answer key हुँदैन। जुन विचार तपाईं सबैभन्दा राम्ररी बुझाउन सक्नुहुन्छ, त्यही सही हो।
**"मलाई विषयबारे थाहा हुनुपर्छ।"** होइन। "I don't know much about this, but I'd guess..." — यो पूरै स्वीकार्य सुरुआत हो; त्यसपछि तर्कसहित अनुमान गर्नुहोस्। तपाईंको ज्ञान होइन, भाषा जाँचिन्छ।
**"Part 1 मा जस्तै छोटा उत्तर।"** होइन। Part 3 का उत्तर ४-६ वाक्यका, ३०-४५ सेकेन्डका हुन्छन्। Examiner ले चाहेमा आफैं रोक्नुहुन्छ; दुई वाक्यपछि आफैं नरोकिनुहोस्।

title: Part 3 का प्रश्नका ८ प्रकार
blocks: Part 2 जस्तै Part 3 पनि predictable छ — topic होइन, **प्रश्नका प्रकार**। Topic जे भए पनि examiner ले यिनै ८ प्रकारका प्रश्न सोध्नुहुन्छ। हरेकलाई चिन्न सक्नुभयो भने उत्तरको भाषा पहिल्यै तयार हुन्छ।
Do you think...? Should...? Is it better to...?
I'd say / I tend to think / I'm inclined to believe / on balance
Why do people...? What makes...? Why is ... popular?
the main reason is / it's largely because / one factor is / this is partly down to
What effect does ... have on...? How does ... influence...?
this leads to / as a result / one consequence is / it tends to make people
How is ... different from...? Old vs young? City vs village?
whereas / while / unlike / on the one hand... on the other / far more likely to
Has ... changed? How was it different in the past?
used to / these days / there's been a shift towards / a generation ago
Will ... in the future? How might ... change?
I imagine / it's likely that / we may well see / I doubt whether / in the next decade or so
How can we...? What should the government do?
one option would be / the government could / a more effective approach might be / it would help if
Advantages/disadvantages? Is it a good thing?
the upside is / a major drawback / it cuts both ways / the benefits outweigh

title: A.R.E + Balance: Part 3 को Framework
blocks: Part A र B को A.R.E यहाँ पनि काम गर्छ — केवल एउटा चौथो चरण थपिन्छ। Part 3 मा examiner ले तपाईं कुनै विषयको **एकभन्दा बढी पक्ष** देख्न सक्नुहुन्छ कि सक्नुहुन्न भनेर हेर्न चाहनुहुन्छ। त्यसैले आफ्नो उत्तर एउटा "तर" ले टुंग्याउनुहोस् — अर्को पक्ष, कुनै शर्त, वा कुनै अपवाद।

**A.R.E + B**
**A — Answer:** स्पष्ट विचार, पहिलो वाक्यमै। (Part 1 भन्दा अलि बढी hedged: "I'd say", "generally")

**R — Reason:** किन — एक वा दुईवटा कारण, सामान्य मान्छे/समाजबारे कुरा गर्दै।

**E — Example:** एउटा ठोस उदाहरण — आफ्नै देश, चिनेको कोही, कुनै trend।

**B — Balance:** "Having said that..." / "Of course, it depends..." / "That's not to say..." — अर्को पक्ष, एक-दुई वाक्यमा।

**Q:** Should schools teach practical skills like cooking or repairing things?
**A:** I think they should, yes — at least the basics.
**R:** The main reason is that these are skills everyone needs, regardless of what career they end up in, and a lot of families simply don't pass them on anymore because parents are working long hours.
**E:** In my country, for instance, plenty of university students can solve calculus problems but can't cook a meal or change a fuse, and they end up either dependent on others or spending money they don't have.
**B:** Having said that, I wouldn't want it to eat into academic time — maybe an hour a week would be enough, rather than a whole subject.
यी चार चरणले तपाईं एउटै उत्तरमा यी सबै देखाउनुहुन्छ: opinion language, cause language, एउटा उदाहरण (LR को मौका), र contrast (GRA — 'although', 'whereas', conditional)। Band 7 को Part 3 उत्तर यही हो।
Having said that, / Then again, / That said, / Mind you, / On the flip side,
It really depends on..., / As long as..., / Provided that..., / Unless...
That's not to say..., / Of course, there are exceptions — / This doesn't apply to everyone;
To some extent, / Up to a point, / In most cases, though not all,
I think the answer is somewhere in the middle. / It's probably a case of both. / The ideal would be a mix of...

Part 3 मा "Governments must ban cars" जस्तो भन्दा अपरिपक्व सुनिन्छ। "I think governments should probably look at restricting cars in city centres" — विचार उही, तर सोचविचार गर्ने मान्छेको भाषामा। Band 7+ का लागि यो hedging अनिवार्य छ:
People tend to be less active than they used to be.
It's quite likely to happen. / I'd expect that to happen.
Most people would probably agree that... / There's a general feeling that...
This can be problematic in some ways. / I'm not sure this is entirely a good thing.
The internet is arguably one of the main reasons. / I'd put a lot of it down to the internet.
Part 3 मा तपाईंले कहिल्यै नसोचेका प्रश्न पक्कै आउँछन्। त्यस्तो बेला तीनवटा बाटा छन् — सबै स्वीकार्य छन्; चुप लाग्नु स्वीकार्य छैन:
**सोचेर अनुमान गर्नुहोस्:** "That's not something I've thought about, but I'd imagine... because..."
**आफ्नै अनुभवबाट सामान्यीकरण गर्नुहोस्:** "I can only really speak from what I've seen in my own family, but there..."
**प्रश्नलाई साँघुरो बनाउनुहोस्:** "It probably depends a lot on the country. In mine, ..."
Examiner लाई "I don't know" मात्र भनेर रोकिन मिल्दैन — तर "I don't know, but..." भनेर अगाडि बढ्न मिल्छ।

title: Worked Example: एउटै topic मा पूरा Part 3
blocks: तल एउटा Part 2 topic बाट आएको पूरा Part 3 छ — ८ प्रकारमध्ये ६ प्रकारका प्रश्न, हरेकको उत्तर A.R.E + B मा। उत्तरहरूको लम्बाइमा ध्यान दिनुहोस्: ४-६ वाक्य।
**Part 2 topic थियो: Describe a journey you took by public transport that you remember well.**

Q1 (Reason): Why do some people prefer public transport to driving?
A: I'd say it comes down to cost and stress, mostly. Owning a car is enormously expensive once you add fuel, parking and repairs, whereas a bus or metro pass is a fraction of that. On top of that, in a congested city, sitting on a train reading is far less draining than sitting in traffic gripping a steering wheel. My cousin actually sold his car last year for exactly that reason. Of course, this only holds where public transport is decent — if the buses are unreliable, people will drive no matter the cost.
Q2 (Compare): How is travelling by public transport different in cities and in the countryside?
A: They're almost two different worlds. In cities, the issue is usually overcrowding — the transport exists, but there's too much demand for it, so rush hour is unpleasant. In rural areas, it's the opposite: services are so infrequent that missing one bus can mean waiting three hours. Where my grandparents live, there are two buses a day, so people plan their whole week around them. Having said that, rural journeys tend to be more pleasant when they do happen — you actually get a seat and a view.
Q3 (Past vs Now): Has public transport in your country changed in recent years?
A: Quite dramatically, at least in the capital. A generation ago it was entirely buses — old, crowded, with no fixed timetable. Now there's a metro line, and it's changed people's expectations: for the first time, a journey has a predictable length. That said, outside the capital things have moved much more slowly, so the gap between the big city and everywhere else has, if anything, widened.
Q4 (Solution): What could governments do to encourage more people to use public transport?
A: The most effective thing would probably be reliability rather than price. People will pay a reasonable fare if they know the bus will actually come. So investing in proper timetables, dedicated bus lanes and real-time tracking apps would do more than subsidies. Singapore is often cited as an example where this works. I'd add, though, that carrots alone aren't enough — some cities have only succeeded when they also made driving less convenient, through congestion charges or parking limits.
Q5 (Evaluate): What are the disadvantages of relying on public transport?
A: The obvious one is loss of control — you're tied to someone else's schedule and route, which is a real problem if you work irregular hours or have young children to carry around. There's also the comfort issue; a packed bus in forty-degree heat is nobody's idea of a good start to the day. And for people with mobility problems, a lot of systems simply aren't accessible. On balance, though, I'd argue these are problems of poor implementation rather than of public transport itself.
Q6 (Predict): How do you think people will travel around cities in fifty years?
A: I'd imagine private car ownership will have dropped sharply, at least in cities. Between shared electric vehicles, better rail and possibly self-driving shuttles, owning a car that sits parked ninety percent of the time will seem wasteful, the way owning a landline seems now. I'm less sure about the timeline — these things always take longer than the headlines suggest. And I doubt it'll happen evenly; wealthier cities will get there first, and places like mine might still be catching up.
प्रश्न सामान्य मान्छेबारे हुँदा पनि Part 1 मा जस्तै आफ्नै कुरा गर्नु ("I use the bus every day because...")।
"People", "most families", "in my country" बाट सुरु गर्नुहोस्; आफ्नो उदाहरण E चरणमा मात्र प्रयोग गर्नुहोस्।
A.R.E + B — चारवटै चरण पार नगरेसम्म नरोकिनुहोस्।
एउटा मात्र विचार, एउटा मात्र पक्ष।
Balance चरण अनिवार्य छ — complex grammar देखाउने ठाउँ यही हो।
"It's a good question" भनेर समय खेर फाल्नु, अनि त्यसपछि पनि भूमिका बाँध्नु।
एउटा filler phrase, त्यसपछि सीधै A मा।
Examiner को counter-argument अगाडि हार मान्नु ("But some people say..." सुन्नेबित्तिकै आफ्नो विचार बदल्नु)।
तपाईं आफ्नो विचारमा टिक्न सक्नुहुन्छ कि सक्नुहुन्न भनेर examiner ले जाँच्दै हुनुहुन्छ। "That's a fair point, but I'd still say..." — आफ्नो विचार कायम राख्नुहोस् र भाषा फैलाउनुहोस्।

title: Part 2 र 3 को अभ्यास कसरी गर्ने
blocks: **दिनमा एउटा cue card** (Part D बाट)। १ मिनेट note — phone मा timer लगाएर। २ मिनेट talk — record गरेर।
**Recording सुन्दा तीनवटा प्रश्न:** २ मिनेट पुग्यो? पाँचवटै चरण थिए? Past tense ठीक थियो?
**उही card का Part 3 प्रश्नहरू** (Part D मा हरेक card सँगै दिइएका) — हरेकको उत्तर A.R.E + B मा, ३०-४५ सेकेन्ड।
**हप्तामा एउटा full mock:** साथी वा परिवारको कोही examiner बन्छ — Part 1 देखि Part 3 सम्म, १२ मिनेट, record गरेर।
**चार हप्तापछि आफ्नो पहिलो हप्ताको recording सुन्नुहोस्।** फरक तपाईं आफैं सुन्नुहुनेछ — र परीक्षाको दिन तपाईंको आत्मविश्वासको स्रोत यही हुनेछ।

title: परीक्षाअघिको हप्ता: Checklist
blocks: किताब सकियो। अब यसलाई score मा बदल्ने अन्तिम सात दिन बाँकी छन्।
Part A का "10 Speaking Tips" फेरि पढ्नुहोस्। आफ्नो सबैभन्दा पुरानो recording सुन्नुहोस्, त्यसपछि सबैभन्दा नयाँ — फरक सुन्नुहोस्। तपाईंको आत्मविश्वास त्यही हो।
Part B: १० वटा random topic, हरेकमा २ वटा प्रश्न, तीनवटा strategy प्रयोग गरेर। आफूलाई record गर्नुहोस् र 'umm' मात्र गन्नुहोस्।
Part D बाट ४ वटा cue card, चारवटा फरक category बाट, timer लगाएर। हरेक card का Part 3 प्रश्नको उत्तर A.R.E + B मा दिनुहोस्।
Full mock: साथी examiner बनेर, १२ मिनेट, Part 1→3, record गरेर। फेरि सुन्नुहोस् र आफूलाई Part A का band descriptor सँग तुलना गर्नुहोस्।
Pronunciation को दिन: गाह्रा आवाजका जोडी, १० मिनेट shadowing, र stress र intonation का लागि मात्र एउटा Part 2 talk।
दोस्रो full mock, फरक topic मा। Part A को "बंगाली भाषीहरूले गर्ने १० गल्ती" सूची एक पटक ठूलो स्वरमा पढ्नुहोस्।
**नयाँ केही होइन।** Part A को "परीक्षाको दिन" अध्याय पढ्नुहोस्। ID, test centre को ठेगाना र लुगा तयार पार्नुहोस्। कसैसँग अंग्रेजीमा १५ मिनेट आरामसँग कुरा गर्नुहोस्। चाँडै सुत्नुहोस्।

एक घण्टाअघिदेखि अंग्रेजी मात्र। कोठामा पस्नुअघि तीन पटक गहिरो सास लिनुहोस्। पहिलो वाक्य स्पष्ट बनाउनुहोस्, र मुस्कुराउँदै भन्नुहोस्। उत्तरको बीचमा रोकिनुपरे अंग्रेजीमै रोकिनुहोस्। अन्त्यमा "Thank you"। बाँकी तपाईंलाई थाहा छ।

**अन्तिम कुरा:** Examiner तपाईंको विरोधमा हुनुहुन्न। उहाँ तपाईंलाई ११ मिनेट अंग्रेजी बोलेको सुन्न त्यहाँ बस्नुभएको हो, र उहाँको काम तपाईं के गर्न सक्नुहुन्छ भनेर पत्ता लगाउनु हो। तपाईंको काम उहाँलाई त्यो सुन्न दिनु मात्र हो। यो किताब त्यसलाई सजिलो बनाउन हो। बाँकी — तपाईंले गरेको तयारी — तपाईंकै हो।
